garden.detail: Garden: about 12 in wide × 5 in deep; height adjusts from 8 to 19 in. Allow access for refilling, space for leaves and a nearby outlet.

microkit.detail: Use one tray at a time. Leave open space above for shoots and access for watering. A dim spot also needs the separate standing light.

pot.detail: Each pot is 8 × 8 × 6.7 in. Allow extra width for saucers and leaves; two pots need more than a 16 × 8 in strip. Herbs may need larger pots as they mature.

bag.detail: Bag: 12 in diameter × 9.5 in high. Tiny Tim grows about 15–20 in above the mix. Leave room around the plant and protect the surface from drainage.

tray.detail: Allow roughly 11 × 11 in for a nested tray set, plus access for watering and space above the shoots. A dim spot also needs the separate standing light.

tomato.timingNote: Tiny Tim variety estimate; allow seed-starting time too, usually 6–8 weeks before transplanting. Weather and light change timing.
tomato.scale: One plant for small, fresh tomato picks.
tomato.care: Check moisture daily; feed established plants according to the product label.
start: Start a few seeds ¼ inch deep in moist mix and a warm, bright spot.
Keep one strong plant for your grow bag. Move it outside gradually after frost risk has passed.
Give it 6–8 hours of direct sun; check water daily and pick ripe fruit.

lettuce.timingNote: Baby leaves first; a fuller Buttercrunch head takes longer. Window light and heat can delay or reduce harvest.
lettuce.scale: Two small plants for fresh leaves to add to meals.
lettuce.care: Keep mix evenly moist and protect leaves from excessive heat.
start: Sow a few seeds near the surface, following the packet depth.
Thin to one lettuce plant per pot; keep the mix moist and the plants well lit.
Pick outer leaves once large enough, leaving at least half the plant growing.

salad.timingNote: From sowing, depending on the varieties selected and growing conditions.
salad.scale: Small handfuls of baby leaves to add to a salad.
salad.care: Keep mix moist and avoid overheating at hot glass.
start: Choose two varieties from the collection and sow them in separate pots.
Thin baby-leaf crops to their packet spacing and keep the mix evenly moist.
Cut young outer leaves, leaving the center to grow; sow again for later crops.

basil.timingNote: From seed, once plants are established. Warmth, light and variety affect timing.
basil.scale: Fresh leaves for garnishes and cooking; larger batches take more plants.
basil.care: Check moisture and pinch growing tips to encourage branching.
start: Sow basil ¼ inch deep in moist potting mix.
Thin to one strong plant per starter pot and keep it warm and well lit.
Pinch above a pair of leaves once established; upsize the pot as the plant grows.

herbs.timingNote: Basil can give earlier picks; slower perennial herbs take longer. Follow each packet rather than one date for all twelve varieties.
herbs.scale: Start two favorite herbs for fresh cooking additions.
herbs.care: Keep varieties in separate pots so watering can match each herb.
start: Choose two herbs you will actually cook with and follow their packet sowing depths.
Give each its own starter pot and the light it needs; thin crowded seedlings.
Pick lightly once established and move larger herbs into bigger pots.

radish.timingNote: For small spring radishes in suitable conditions. Low window light can slow root development.
radish.scale: A small batch of crunchy roots; sow again for the next batch.
radish.care: Keep moisture even and give each root its own space.
start: Sow directly in the final pot, about ½ inch deep.
Thin seedlings to about 2 inches apart and water evenly.
Check roots at harvest size and pull promptly; sow a fresh batch for more.

micro.timingNote: Broccoli and radish research estimates are 8–12 days under controlled conditions. Home window light can take longer.
micro.scale: One tray of young shoots for sandwiches, toppings and salads.
micro.care: Check moisture daily; keep the medium moist and drain excess water.
start: Clean the tray, moisten the medium and spread seed evenly; follow the kit or seed instructions.
Uncover after germination and move into bright light. Water from below once roots establish.
Cut shoots above the medium with clean scissors, then wash before eating. Re-sow for the next crop.

pea.timingNote: Research estimates are 8–10 days in controlled conditions. Variety and home conditions can take longer.
pea.scale: A tray of young pea shoots to add to meals.
pea.care: Check moisture daily; drain away excess water.
start: Soak seed for about 6 hours, then sow in clean, moist medium; follow the packet if it differs.
Cover during germination, then uncover and provide bright light.
Cut shoots above the medium with clean scissors and wash before eating.

basil-kit.timingNote: Manufacturer’s range from planting the pods; growth depends on temperature and care.
basil-kit.scale: Three basil plants for fresh additions to cooking.
basil-kit.care: Top up the reservoir as indicated and trim basil as it grows.
start: Insert the three basil pods, fill the reservoir and plug the garden in.
Use the included germination domes as directed; remove them when seedlings reach them.
Keep the light above the plants and refill when needed. Pinch basil once established.
